fields.topology_type: Single-client / multi-server request/reply application protocol; the underlying transport (RTU/ASCII on EIA/TIA-485 multi-drop, RTU/ASCII on EIA/TIA-232 point-to-point, or Modbus TCP on switched Ethernet) determines the physical interconnect.

supported_topologies.name: RS-485 multi-drop (Modbus RTU / ASCII)
supported_topologies.description: Single master (client) + up to 247 individual servers (addresses 1..247) on a shared half-duplex differential pair. Broadcast (address 0) reaches all servers; servers do not reply to broadcasts.

supported_topologies.name: RS-232 point-to-point (Modbus RTU / ASCII)
supported_topologies.description: One client + one server on a 2-wire async serial link (full-duplex). Optionally with the 6 RS-232 modem handshakes (CTS/RTS/DSR/DTR/DCD/RI) — but MODBUS itself uses none of them.

supported_topologies.name: Switched Ethernet (Modbus TCP)
supported_topologies.description: Each MODBUS endpoint sits behind a TCP socket on its own MAC + IP address. The server reserves TCP port 502. Multiple clients may simultaneously connect to a single server; each connection is a separate TCP context.

supported_topologies.name: Modbus gateway (TCP ↔ RTU bridge)
supported_topologies.description: A gateway terminates a TCP front-end and originates RTU traffic on one or more downstream serial sub-networks. MBAP.Unit_ID selects which serial address to forward to. Failure modes 0x0A / 0x0B are reserved for gateway-specific exceptions.

supported_topologies.name: Modbus PLUS (HDLC token-passing, legacy)
supported_topologies.description: Modicon-proprietary peer-to-peer network that carries the MODBUS PDU. Each station holds the token in turn and may initiate a transaction; superseded by Modbus TCP in modern deployments.

master_slave_role_summary.role: Client (a.k.a. master in legacy RTU/ASCII terminology)
master_slave_role_summary.description: Sole initiator of transactions. Builds the request PDU, sends it on the chosen transport, awaits the response. On serial transports, only one master per bus.

Responds to addressed requests; never initiates. On Modbus TCP, a single device may simultaneously act as a server for one connection and a client for another, but within any one transaction the roles are fixed.
Bridges a TCP front-end to a downstream serial sub-network (or another TCP segment). Translates between MBAP-framed and RTU/ASCII-framed ADUs; routes by Unit ID.

fields.interconnect_role: MODBUS itself defines no routing or switching — every transaction is unicast addressed by RTU address (serial) or unit ID + IP/port (TCP). Routing across transports is handled by Modbus gateways that translate the ADU framing and forward the unchanged PDU.

ordering_guarantees.within_a_message: Bytes appear on the wire in transport-specific order: Address → PDU → CRC (RTU); ':' → ADDR → FC → DATA → LRC → CR LF (ASCII); MBAP → PDU (TCP). Multi-byte numerical quantities are big-endian.
ordering_guarantees.across_messages: On serial transports there is at most one transaction in flight at a time (request → response → next). On Modbus TCP, multiple transactions may be in flight on a single socket, disambiguated by Transaction ID; responses may arrive in any order relative to requests.

fields.memory_vs_peripheral_regions: MODBUS exposes 4 logical data tables (Discrete Inputs, Coils, Input Registers, Holding Registers) each addressed 0..65535 in the PDU. The mapping of these logical addresses to physical RAM / I/O is vendor-specific.

slave_classification.polling_target: Client periodically reads Holding/Input Registers to acquire process data; one common pattern is 'poll every 100 ms'.
slave_classification.event_target: Modbus over UDP / TCP / serial does not natively support unsolicited server-to-client notifications; servers act only on request. To get event-driven behavior, clients poll Discrete Inputs or use vendor-defined extensions.
slave_classification.gateway_target: Server can be addressed indirectly via a gateway by setting MBAP.Unit_ID to the downstream serial address.

broadcast_topology_rtu_ascii.valid_function_codes: Writes that can be applied unconditionally — typical: FC 0x05, 0x06, 0x0F, 0x10, 0x16.
broadcast_topology_rtu_ascii.invalid_for_broadcast: All Read codes (FC 0x01..0x04, 0x07, 0x08, 0x0B, 0x0C, 0x11, 0x14, 0x18, 0x2B/MEI14) — no useful response possible.
broadcast_topology_rtu_ascii.server_action: Process the request; do NOT transmit any response.
broadcast_topology_rtu_ascii.client_post_broadcast: Wait T_broadcast_interval (≥ T3.5 silence) before next frame.

gateway_routing_topology.tcp_front_end: Listens on TCP port 502; demultiplexes by source IP / TCP-connection.
gateway_routing_topology.unit_id_routing: MBAP.Unit_ID selects the downstream addressed device. Some gateways use Unit_ID = 0xFF for the gateway itself.
gateway_routing_topology.serial_back_end: Originates RTU (or ASCII) frames toward the addressed device.
gateway_routing_topology.failure_modes: Gateway emits exception 0x0A GATEWAY PATH UNAVAILABLE if it cannot allocate a path; 0x0B GATEWAY TARGET DEVICE FAILED TO RESPOND if the target device times out.
